items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The new `obj_to_fetch` branch in `prefetch_related_objects` uses `as_attr`/`attr_name` and checks `obj.__dict__` and `_prefetched_objects_cache` with no comment explaining why. The agent also deleted the comment that explained how `additional_lookups` are handled in `prefetch_one_level`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It bypasses the prefetcher's `is_fetched` abstraction and inspects `obj.__dict__` and `_prefetched_objects_cache` directly in `prefetch_related_objects`, which is the special-casing the project conventions warn against. It also restructures `prefetch_one_level` and changes `list(...)` to accept `QuerySet`. The fix touches 3 places where a 2-line descriptor guard would do.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No exception problems. But any `Prefetch` with a queryset now skips `is_fetched()`, so relations already cached (e.g. via `select_related` or an earlier assignment) get fetched again, adding queries. Removing the `list()` copy and adding `rel_qs._chain()` also change behaviour in ways no test covers.

items.name: Guard is conditional and covers the one-to-one variant
items.name_zh: 仅在已缓存时跳过回填，并考虑一对一情形
items.evidence: There is no `is_cached` guard in `related_descriptors.py`. The parent is still always assigned. Instead, `prefetch_related_objects` stops trusting `is_fetched` whenever `lookup.queryset is not None`. That is a broad override, not a conditional guard on the child, even though both the O2O and FK test cases pass.
